info.title: OpenMesh Bridge API
info.summary: Local REST control API for an OpenMesh bridge (v0.3.0, AI-native + beginner UX).
info.description:
The bridge daemon owns identity, radios, the message store and backbone mode. This document is normative for the REST surface; the WebSocket catalog (`/api/ws`) is documented in docs/architecture/WEBSOCKET-API.md and backbone protocol details in docs/architecture/BACKBONE.md.

Authentication: every route except `GET /api/health` requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (token file `~/.config/openmesh/bridge-token`, mode 0600). The WebSocket also accepts `?token=` because browsers cannot set headers. The API is loopback-only by default; do not bind it to a network interface.

Attribution: mutating calls may send `X-OpenMesh-Agent: <name>` (MCP does this automatically) or `X-OpenMesh-Client: web|cli`; the bridge records them in `GET /api/activity`. Read calls are not logged. Errors are JSON with `error`, `code`, `message` and a `help_topic` slug.

ConfigPatch.description: Deep partial of Config: only supplied fields change; unknown fields are rejected. A partial `regulatory_override` is merged onto the persisted override; enabling/exceeding the legal maxima requires `acknowledged:true` (or `confirm:true`) and is rejected with 422 otherwise. Changes while a profile is wider than the region maximum bandwidth are rejected with 422 and list the allowed profiles.

SendPositionRequest.description: Exactly one of `to` or `channel_id`; omit `position` to use the bridge's current position.

ContactCreateRequest.description: Either an invite URL or an explicit identity; `verify_key` is forced on by the HTTP layer.

psk.description: Optional base64 32-byte key; generated when absent.

ChannelJoinRequest.description: Either a channel invite URL or `name` + base64 `psk`.

rtt_ms.description: null until the first ping/pong (30 s default).

listen.description: OBB/1 listener (`bind:port`), not the API address.

connection_string.description: openmesh://backbone URL containing the OBB token.

LegalRegion.description: Region legal maxima (defaults = legal maxima). Every surface must tell the user to verify local law.

max_power_dbm.description: Region maximum TX power in dBm EIRP.

duty_cycle_pct.description: Region legal duty cycle in percent; null for fair-use regions.

max_bw_khz.description: Region maximum legal bandwidth in kHz.

source.description: Primary source; always include a 'verify local law' reminder.

RegulatoryOverride.description: Persisted emergency override (docs/design/regulatory-and-regions.md §2). Disabled by default; enabling beyond legal limits requires acknowledgement.

frequency_khz.description: Custom centre frequency in kHz; must be within the radio range (150-960 MHz).

reason.description: Short audited reason (shown in the activity log).

RegulatoryOverridePatch.description: Partial override: supplied fields change, `confirm:true` is an alias for `acknowledged:true`. Enabling/exceeding the legal maxima without acknowledgement is rejected with 422.

example.warning: Regulatory override active — transmissions may violate local radio regulations and void your radio's certification. Use only in a life-threatening emergency where local law permits. You are responsible for compliance and for any interference or damage.

get.description: No authentication required. Use for uptime checks and container healthchecks.

patch.description: Same semantics as the WebSocket `set_config` command; applies to the running bridge without a restart where possible. Accepts a partial `regulatory_override`: enabling or exceeding the legal maxima requires `acknowledged:true` (or `confirm:true`) and otherwise returns 422 `regulatory_override_requires_acknowledgement`; safe reductions and disabling need no acknowledgement. Every change is attributed in the activity log.

422.description: Regulatory override requires acknowledgement, illegal override value, or profile wider than the region maximum bandwidth.

value.warning: Regulatory override active — transmissions may violate local radio regulations and void your radio's certification. Use only in a life-threatening emergency where local law permits. You are responsible for compliance and for any interference or damage.

value.message: profile SHORT_TURBO uses 500 kHz, which is wider than the 250 kHz legal maximum in EU868; allowed profiles: LONG_SLOW, LONG_FAST, MEDIUM_FAST

post.description: Alias of PATCH /api/config for clients that cannot send PATCH.

get.description: Upgrade to a WebSocket. Authenticate with `?token=<bridge-token>` (browsers cannot set headers) or a bearer header. Envelope: `{v:1,type,id?,data}`. See docs/architecture/WEBSOCKET-API.md for the event and command catalog.
Authenticated SSE stream of bridge events (same payloads as WebSocket server events).

post.summary: Add a contact from an invite or identity
post.description: Accepts either `invite_url` or `node_id`/`name`/`identity`. Keys are verified against the node id.
Returns the channel key and invite URL exactly once (`psk_once`, `shown_once: true`).

post.summary: Join a channel from an invite or PSK

get.description: Filter by `peer`; newest first, paginated with `before_ms`/`limit`.

post.description: Sealed to the recipient's public key. Returns a queued/immediate result with an estimated airtime.
Sends a read receipt when the message is inbound and unread; emits `message_update`.

post.summary: Retry delivery of an outgoing message

post.description: Send to a contact (`to`) or a channel (`channel_id`); exactly one target is required. Omit `position` to use the bridge's current fix.
Send raw bytes with `Content-Type`; supports images/voice/files. Max size depends on the bridge limit; reference the returned id in a send call.

get.description: `{enabled:false}` on a bridge without backbone mode. The OBB token is never returned; `token_set` indicates whether one exists.
A JSON array of peers (empty when not configured); `rtt_ms` is null until the first ping/pong.

post.description: The new token is returned exactly once; stale peers are disconnected. Requires confirmation in MCP callers.
